newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Reuters chief executive Job sees Internet security risk.
newsitem.headline: Reuters chief executive Job sees Internet security risk.

text.p: Peter Job, chief executive of news and information group Reuters Holdings Plc, said on Thursday the Internet had security risks which could not be eliminated.

Job told a meeting of the Irish Business and Employers Confederation (IBEC) that moving to the Internet was like "moving from a crowded city centre, with expensive turnpike roads leading into it, to a dispersed community with big suburbs everywhere."
"But the suburbs have problems -- such as security and traffic jams. Burglary is rife in the suburbs. Ways of policing them will be found but will never go away," he said in prepared remarks.
"Use of the Internet will be hedged around by security risks, which can be contained but not eliminated," he told IBEC's annual business conference, held in Dublin castle.

"The concept of the Intranet, with limited interfacing to the outside world, is a prime means of defending security," he told the conference, which included as speakers Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn and central bank governor Maurice O'Connell.
Job said the more popular suburbs became, the more traffic jams would increase.
"Internet does not necessarily bring insoluble traffic problems with it because each new home owner brings a section of highway with him," Job said.
"However, the current Internet pathways are like busy crossroads without traffic lights. Technical solutions are there, including push technology," he said.
"This emerging technology has huge ramifications for making the Internet efficient and useful on a consistent basis," he said.
Job said the new world should be good for Ireland, but the cost of infrastructure will be important as communications links are the cobweb of the 'Net'.
